title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 357
paragraphs: Up to this point in the story, it was the Egyptians and their priests who gave the account, declaring that from the first king down to this priest of Hephaistos who reigned last, there had been three hundred and forty-one generations of men, and in that span there had been the same number of chief priests and kings. Now three hundred generations of men equal ten thousand years, since a hundred years is three generations; and in the forty-one generations that remain — those I mean which were added to the three hundred — there are one thousand three hundred and forty years. So in the period of eleven thousand three hundred and forty years, they said, no god had arisen in human form, nor even before or after that time, among the remaining kings who arose in Egypt, did they report that anything of the kind had happened. During this time they said the sun had moved four times from his accustomed place of rising — where he now sets he had twice risen, and where he now rises he had twice set; and in the meantime nothing in Egypt had changed from its usual state, neither in the produce of the earth, nor in what comes to them from the river, nor in matters of disease or death.
